description: Z.O.S.M.A. (Zero-gravity Operational Support & Medical Agent) — An autonomous, offline-first astronaut health monitoring & countermeasure system for deep-space missions against spaceflight hazards.
summary:
ZOSMA is health monitoring software that gives every astronaut a simple traffic light for their own health. It combines quick daily logs with readings from onboard devices such as CSA’s Bio-Monitor smart shirt, and covers three areas: musculoskeletal (muscle, bone and body mass), cardiovascular and aerobic fitness, and the habitat (radiation dose, solar events, noise, cabin CO₂ and sleep). ZOSMA compares each value with the astronaut’s own pre-flight baseline and recent trend, not just a population normal range. Each result is green, yellow or red, with a plain explanation, a next step pre-approved by flight surgeons, and when to measure again.
This answers the challenge: it helps astronauts assess their own health and decide when a result needs the crew medical officer or flight surgeons. It supports decisions; it does not diagnose.
We tested it on real data. With NASA OSDR RadLab measurements from the ISS, ZOSMA flagged eight straight yellow hours during the May 2024 solar storm, when the dose rate reached 7.7 times its baseline. On missions to the Moon and Mars, crews need this early warning. Like its namesake star, ZOSMA helps guide every crew home.
details:
OVERVIEW & WHAT IT DOES

Z.O.S.M.A. (Zero-gravity Operational Support & Medical Agent) is a 100% offline-capable onboard medical decision-support system designed for deep-space Artemis lunar and Mars missions, where one-way communication delays (up to 20+ minutes) prevent real-time Flight Surgeon intervention. Built for crew members without a medical background, Z.O.S.M.A. converts multi-system telemetry and daily crew check-ins into intuitive GREEN / YELLOW / RED status lights, plain-language physiological explanations, a 3-Step Crew Guidance Protocol (1. How to Measure, 2. What It Means, 3. Action Protocol), and an automated Closed-Loop Triage & Regimen Scheduler.

HOW IT WORKS (4-LAYER DECISION ENGINE & 5 SUBSYSTEMS)

Every incoming measurement passes through a 4-stage decision pipeline (Worst Result Wins):

- Layer 0 (Quality Gatekeeper): Filters out corrupted sensor packets, low Mini OCT signal-to-noise ratios, stuck habitat sensors (>=24h flat CO2), and mis-sorted blood differentials before clinical evaluation.

- Layer 1 (Fixed Clinical & NASA-STD-3001 Rules): Enforces acute aerospace safety limits and emergency fast-tracks.

- Layer 2 (Personal Pre-Flight Baseline): Compares readings against each astronaut's own pre-flight baseline (±2 SD or Δ%) to detect subtle deconditioning missed by standard terrestrial lab ranges.

- Layer 3 (Longitudinal Trend Projection): Computes linear regression slopes (dY/dt) to forecast "days until red," escalating metrics to YELLOW days before crossing dangerous limits.

Five integrated domain modules continuously exchange context via a Cross-Module Telemetry Bus:

1. Musculoskeletal: E4D bone stimulus index, velocity-based training (VBT) squat fatigue, ultrasound muscle cross-sectional area, SLAMMD body mass, and bone turnover markers (NTX, CTX, P1NP).

2. Cardiovascular & Aerobic: 11 indicators (M1–M11) including resting HR, PTT blood pressure, SpO2, Holter 24h PVC burden, LBNP/stand orthostatic tolerance, CEVIS 150W HR drift, ultrasound GLS cardiac strain, internal jugular vein (IJV) clot screening, and Dill & Costill plasma volume shift (%ΔPV).

3. Neuro-Ocular & Vestibular (SANS): Bilateral (OD/OS) Mini OCT evaluation (ΔTRT, ΔV_ONH, RNFL, hyperopic shift), ultrasound optic nerve sheath diameter (ONSD), and gravity-transition-aware vestibular tracking (VOR gain, ocular counter-rolling, motion sickness, tandem walk).

4. Immune, Endocrine & Metabolic: Oral temperature, 9-symptom checklist, finger-prick WBC/lymphocyte/neutrophil differential, post-SPE 48-hour lymphocyte tracking, salivary VZV/EBV viral reactivation, sleep/stress load, CRP/IL-6, Vitamin D3, and renal stone hydration guard.

5. Radiation, Acoustics & Closed-Habitat Environment: 17 NASA-STD-3001 cards covering DOSTEL area radiation with South Atlantic Anomaly (SAA) masking, personal cumulative dose, NOAA GOES-18 solar proton flux, module/personal acoustic dosimetry, cabin ppCO2, total pressure/O2, T/RH comfort envelope, VOC/ammonia SMAC ratios, water/microbial limits, and PVT-B cognitive alertness.

BENEFITS, CREATIVITY & FACTORS CONSIDERED

- Cross-Module Safety Arbitration: Automatically halts heavy E4D resistance workouts when Cardiovascular or Immune triggers a RED alert, links Solar Particle Events (SPE) to shelter entry + 48h lymphocyte re-checks, and coordinates CO2 scrubbing with SANS ocular monitoring.

- Day-1 Cold-Start Standby & Low Alarm Fatigue: Physiological modules stay in STANDBY at Mission Day 1 until baseline check-ins are logged, preventing false alarms during launch transition.

- Hybrid Real + Literature-Calibrated Data: Validated on real NASA OSDR (OSD-569, OSD-575), NOAA SWPC GOES-18, and PhysioNet (MIT-BIH, PRCP) datasets, paired with synthetic long-duration transit generators and a Developer Mode for full diagnostic stress-testing.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & OFFLINE DESKTOP DEPLOYMENT

- Stack: Python 3.10+, Streamlit, Plotly, Pydantic, Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, PyYAML, custom HTML5/CSS3/SVG/JS SpaceX-inspired bilingual HUD (English & Traditional Chinese), and PyInstaller + pywebview.

- Standalone Windows App: Packaged as a zero-dependency Windows executable (ZOSMA.exe) for offline spacecraft computers.

- GitHub Repository: https://github.com/louis71803/ZOSMA

- Windows Executable Download (GitHub Releases): https://github.com/louis71803/ZOSMA/releases
